NAME: Uncertainty-aware graph convolutional neural network for vibrational free‑energy prediction
TYPE: method

DIRECT_CLAIMS: A graph convolutional neural network predicts vibrational free energies with root‑mean‑square errors of 8.23 meV/atom (training), 11.34 meV/atom (validation) and 12.31 meV/atom (test), and its predictions for MgS and NaH polymorphs match DFT‑computed values across the 200–700 K range.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Screening of approximately 50 000 inorganic crystals with the machine‑learning model identified over 2 000 temperature‑induced solid‑solid polymorphic transitions between 300 K and 600 K, including 130 stable transitions within the technologically relevant 300 K–350 K interval.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Twenty‑one stable polar‑nonpolar transitions are predicted to exhibit relative lattice‑thermal‑conductivity changes of at least 20 % (0.20), ranging up to a 73 % increase for ZrSeO with a conductivity ratio of 1.73.

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Several predicted solid‑solid transitions show large entropy changes exceeding 300 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹ (e.g., Li₃MnF₇: 342.3 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹, PnCl₂: 338.3 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹, Fe₄OF₇: 252.1 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹), while the highest entropy changes (> 400 J K⁻¹ kg⁻¹) are limited to transitions above 450 K and occur exclusively in nonpolar‑nonpolar categories, reducing their relevance for room‑temperature applications.
ARTICLE: Machine Learning-Guided Discovery of Temperature-Induced Solid-Solid Phase Transitions in Inorganic Materials

NAME: Looser convergence tolerances
TYPE: technique

DIRECT_CLAIMS: Accurate conservative, rotationally unconstrained models can be used safely for phonon calculations, though it is recommended to use looser convergence tolerances or enforce rotational averaging when performing free geometry optimizations with unconstrained models, especially with direct-force predictions.
ARTICLE: Pushing the limits of unconstrained machine-learned interatomic potentials
